name: Omphalocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging diagnosis of omphalocele

criteria.description: Presence of a midline abdominal wall defect at the base of the umbilical cord
Herniation of abdominal viscera (e.g., intestines, liver) into a membranous sac
Presence of a translucent membranous sac covering the herniated organs
Prenatal ultrasound showing abdominal wall defect with herniated organs
Identification of associated congenital anomalies (e.g., cardiac defects, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a midline abdominal wall defect with herniation of abdominal organs covered by a membranous sac
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and confirmed by prenatal or postnatal imaging

laboratory: Hypoglycemia in Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome associated cases
Elevated alpha-fetoprotein in maternal serum prenatal screening
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing abdominal wall defect with herniated viscera
Fetal MRI to assess extent of herniation and associated anomalies
Postnatal abdominal X-ray or ultrasound confirming defect and organ position
genetic: Molecular testing for Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (11p15 abnormalities)
other: Physical examination revealing midline abdominal wall defect covered by membranous sac

distinguishingFeatures: Defect is usually right of umbilicus, not midline
No covering membranous sac over herniated organs
Herniation involves only intestines, rarely liver
Smaller defect with protrusion of omentum or bowel covered by skin

redFlags: Rupture of the membranous sac leading to evisceration and infection
Associated major cardiac or chromosomal anomalies
Respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia or large herniation
references: Moore KL, Persaud TVN. The Developing Human: Clinically Oriented Embryology. 11th Edition. Elsevier; 2015.
Sadler TW. Langman’s Medical Embryology. 14th Edition. Wolters Kluwer; 2019.
